ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $6.27 to the rider (NS-7) for the unexempt off-route segment on this RydeTAXI metered trip
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI trip, Clarke Quay → Sentosa Beach Station, metered fare $31.22 [F7]. The optimal route is 7.7 km / 16.5 min; the car drove 13.0 km / 28.8 min, +5.3 km (+69%) [F1][F2]. One off-route segment is recorded (18:34–18:45): 5.53 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, adding 4.45 km, up to 1889 m off the optimal route [F3]. Under RD-1 every such segment is reviewed under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 and, if not excused, is an unexempt deviation [RD-1][F3].

RD-4 (a) is settled against the driver: the trace marks no qualifying LTA incident on the replaced stretch, and the fact table confirms no traffic incidents near the route in the trip window [F14]; a speed-band record alone does not exempt (RD-4(b), MVP) [RD-4][F11][F12][F13]. F11 (Kampong Bahru Road band 2, 10–19 km/h, 18:16–18:34) at most corroborates, and it expires at 18:34, before the segment ends [F11].

RD-5 consent is not made out. The only chat message is the driver's own question at 18:30 — "mind if I go round via Zion Road?" — and the complete chat record contains just that one timestamped message with no rider reply [F8][F9]. The rider's complaint likewise states the driver asked about another road and "I did not reply" [F8]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider raised "no objection" is a claim appearing only in the statement, which is not consent (G11) [F10][RD-5]. A complete chat record with no rider message agreeing before the segment started (18:34) is "counts", not exempt: the ground is consent_after_or_none [RD-5].

RD-3 does not apply: nothing in the record shows a rider message naming a specific place, and no stop is measured in the segment, so there is no rider-named stop to exempt the way there [F8][F3][RD-3].

Amount (RydeTAXI: deviation distance is billed through the meter, so only the unexempt segment's extra km is refunded) [RD-2]: the rate is this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km = $18.37 ÷ 13.03 km = $1.4098/km [F7][F4]. Extra km of the unexempt segment = 5.53 km − 1.08 km = 4.45 km [F3]. 4.45 km × $1.4098/km = $6.2736 → $6.27 [F3][F7][RD-2]. The remaining +0.85 km (the $7.47 excess-distance figure less the segment sum) is unattributed corridor/matching jitter and is not refunded (RD-2) [F4]. The waiting amount $0.11 is a metered waiting unit on RydeTAXI and is not refunded (RD-3(c)) [F5][RD-3].

Flag: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the driver profile shows route disputes upheld = 0 and the trace marks the RD-6 element ✗, so no flag_account [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the driver's chat question, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint — a route/fare argument with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation [F8][F10][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: every element the ruling needs (measured segment, fare breakdown, complete timestamped chat) is present, so evidence_gap is null [F3][F7][F9].

segment_findings.reason: The driver asked at 18:30 whether he could go round via Zion Road; the complete, fully timestamped chat record contains only that message and no rider reply [F8][F9]. The rider agrees in the complaint that she did not reply [F8]. The driver's statement that the rider made no objection is a claim recorded only after the trip and is not consent (G11) [F10]. No rider message agreeing to any route exists before the segment started at 18:34, so the whole 4.45 km extra of this segment is an unexempt deviation [RD-1][RD-5].
